takeaway: Pseudogout: knee effusion with positively birefringent crystals on polarized light; gout is the more common crystal arthropathy.

question.text: A 60-year-old man has knee pain and a moderate effusion. Fluid microscopy shows crystals that are positively birefringent under polarized light. Diagnosis?
question.say: A sixty-year-old man complains of knee pain, and there is a moderate effusion. The fluid is withdrawn, and microscopy shows crystals that are positively birefringent under polarized light. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.text: A 60-year-old man with a painful, swollen knee.
lines.say: This sixty-year-old man has a painful knee.

lines.text: The knee has a moderate effusion.
lines.say: The knee holds a moderate effusion.

lines.text: The syringe withdraws fluid full of crystals.
lines.say: The doctor withdraws the fluid, and the syringe is full of crystals.

lines.text: The crystals are dancing a party in the joint.
lines.say: (laugh) Look at the crystals, they are having a party in the joint!

lines.text: Under polarized light they are positively birefringent.
lines.say: Under polarized light, the crystals are positively birefringent.

lines.text: Crystals in a joint cause synovitis: gout or pseudogout. Gout is more common.
lines.say: Crystals in a joint cause synovitis. There are two main forms, gout and pseudogout. Gout is the more common.

lines.text: Remember: positively birefringent crystals in a knee effusion mean pseudogout.
lines.say: Remember: positively birefringent crystals in a knee effusion mean pseudogout.
